title: Deception of False Prophecy
english: The idea of having a notion is presented, and it is said that the rebuke is just according to those who are esteemed in the highest dignity.

The one who is esteemed in the highest dignity, having been arrayed in my armor, says to the soldier, 'You think the things of barbarians; but I, because you only wish to be seen, being entirely of others.'
It seems that God also speaks about those who are not established in faith, saying that this people honors Him with their lips, but their heart is far from Him (Isaiah 29:13).
They worship Him in vain, keeping the teachings and commandments of men, which are nothing but human traditions.
Time changes the expression to what is beneficial, and some people have rushed into abomination, paying attention to spirits of error and giving their mind to false and deceitful prophecies.
They pay attention to the movement of the stars and pull the healthy and unerring glory, and those who are easy to carry away and prone to deception.
They do not see the things above, but imagine they know the things under the earth, and they deceive themselves, being cowardly, and destroy others with their own heads.
They persuade people to be initiated into their false beliefs, promising knowledge of future things and special divine superiority.
They use deceitful speeches, and the things that are beneath, they hint at with some foolish and deceitful speeches, and the barely collected money is stolen.
For the art of cold and unlawful gains is their guardian, and the writing on the public tablet, they make a false and deceitful marketplace.
Some of the Israelites had become complacent in their fear of God and had begun to despise the Lord's prophetic work.
The prophet Ezekiel received a word from the Lord, which said, 'Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who are prophesying from their own hearts' (Ezekiel 13:2).

The Lord's message was clear: because their words were false and their divinations empty, He would be against them, and He declared that He would stretch out His hand against the prophets who saw false visions and spoke empty words.
Furthermore, the Lord spoke against the women who were weaving a wicked spell of knowledge, turning people's souls away from the truth.
He said, 'Woe to those who sew cushions on every elbow and make veils for every head of every age, to turn souls away' (Ezekiel 13:18).

These women were making souls perish and profaning the Lord's name before His people, all for a handful of barley and a piece of bread, to kill souls that should not die, and to keep alive souls that should not live; when you speak to the people who listen to empty words.
For the truth is that true prophecy does not lead people to follow other laws or empty words, but rather to follow the law of the Lord.
Those who compose speeches that resemble the ones they are accustomed to send out deceitful messages from their workshops of deceit.

They claim to be skilled and wise, having advanced in their craft and precision, but they are deceived about their own affairs and would say they have not experienced the consequences of their actions.
Although it is easy for someone who knows beforehand to guard against and escape the predicted outcome, why do they not run ahead of the dangers of others, despite trusting in their craft?
Their discoveries are rightly considered deceitful, and through them, the truth of our affairs is revealed.
But they say that some of what was said has turned out to be true, and indeed, this is what the scripture says, and what we should be mindful of.
One who is fleeing and being pursued will not make an apology for their crimes, for we do not consider it true that some of what was said has turned out to be true.

The fact that they do not see everything as true would be a clear proof of the disgust that is in them, and it would show that their pursuit is still sinful, and their craft is full of nonsense, and their lesson is laughable.
Human conceptions are often the product of conjecture rather than a genuine pursuit of truth.
Each person's opinions seem to be influenced by their passions and bodily concerns, and they think they can hit the mark, but their boasts are empty, and they are ridiculed by others.

The one who is healthy in their understanding does not boast about one thing, and they are not puffed up, and they do not pretend to have knowledge they do not have, and they do not ask for praise from others.
The holy prophets who were among us did not concern themselves with measuring the movement of the stars or meddling with the needs of elements.
Rather, they received a divine revelation of the Spirit, which enabled them to foresee future events and proclaim them to us from afar.
As a result, their words have proven to be true, and the nature of things has unfolded in time, precisely as they had foretold, for it was God who spoke through them.
The prophets rejected the deadly and mercenary astrological deception, which is based on the ways of the nations.
As the Lord says, we should not learn from the ways of the nations, nor should we fear the signs of the sky, for the thoughts of the nations are vain (Jeremiah 10:2).

The translation tries to follow the original word order as closely as possible, but some adjustments were made to ensure natural literary prose in the author's voice.

The translation of 'φενακισμοῖς' as 'vain deceptions' is based on the context, which suggests false or empty claims rather than cleverness.

title: On Divine Knowledge and the Rejection of Divination
english: We do not occupy ourselves with altar-dwellings, but we allow the voices of the true theologians to possess the glory that lies beyond all things, not attributing such grace to the stars by their very nature. For surely it is not a seemly or exalted thing to enrich our knowledge of future events by peering into what is to come; and how could this be doubtful? For the power to bring existing things forth from non-existence into being resides not in some other created thing but in the same source that upholds all that has already come to be, all that now exists, and even all that is yet to be—the very knowledge of God.

It is no harmless matter to set one’s affection on worthless divinings, as the blessed Moses declares, and indeed more truly, the God of all who spoke through Moses: 'When you enter the land that the Lord your God gives you, you shall not learn to follow the abominations of the nations. There shall not be found among you anyone who burns his son or daughter in fire, who practices divination, observes omens, or consults birds, who is a sorcerer, an enchanter, a ventriloquist, a necromancer, or one who inquires of the dead. For whoever does these things is an abomination to the Lord your God.' And concerning this, he adds: 'You shall be blameless before the Lord your God.' For the nations whom you shall dispossess listen to omens and divinings, but the Lord your God has not dealt with you in this way. Therefore, nothing could be more shameful than the accusations tied to false divination and the giving of heed to omens.

Indeed, this seems paradoxical, for at times God does speak something true through such means, yet He uses it as a torment—like some ordeal placed upon the very foundations of faith—upon those who worship Him, thus testing their trust.

If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you and gives you a sign or wonder, and that sign or wonder comes to pass just as he said, urging you to go and serve other gods you have not known, you must not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer. For the Lord your God is testing you to see whether you love Him with all your heart and all your soul.

But those people, going their own way against themselves, are described as 'wandering and being led astray,' just as it is written. This seems right to them. However, we bake our words in holy fire, remembering the scribe, as it is said: 'You will make straight paths for your feet, and you will direct your ways.' A straight path is one without turning, carried straight toward every good thing; and regarding the false divinings at the exits, we say to be strong, to know, and simply to recognize who is God by nature and truly Lord.

For thus it is necessary to think, and the ancient law through Moses was inscribed, as it is written: 'For the Lord, he says, your God you shall worship, and Him alone you shall serve.' – One God the Father is among us, and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom all things are. – In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was toward God, and God was the Word.

All things came into being through him, and without him not one thing came into being. We do not mean, as some falsely suppose, that the Scriptures teach that the creation of all things through him involves a subordinate or instrumental role, as if some deficiency required the Father to rely on the Logos as a mere instrument to complete the work of creation.

Such ideas are the dregs of an impious mind and the delusions of heterodox madness. But since he is both the wisdom and power of God the Father, through him all things are summoned into existence, and those who are called are preserved in their being, ordered toward well-being and sustained in goodness.

As it is written: 'God did not make death, nor does he take pleasure in the destruction of the living.' There is no realm of Hades established upon the earth. For he made all things to exist, and the generations of the world are meant to be preservations of life.

Yet through the envy of the devil, death entered into the world. Human nature has been led astray, having abandoned reverence toward God, and has thus been brought under the power of sin. Just as sin brings with it the necessity of dying and the acceptance of decay, so too has corruption gained dominion over mortal life.

He heard the decree: 'You are dust, and to dust you shall return.' But concerning the good, the One who is by nature the Creator of all things, it seemed fitting to fashion humanity toward incorruption, to shape the process of salvation with wisdom, so as to restore the original, unblemished beauty that existed from the beginning.
In this way, the only-begotten Son of God, the Logos, has become man. Though he took on the form of our likeness, he remains incapable of being set aside or diminished in his divine nature.
For the nature that transcends all things and stands highest knows no alteration.

Having remained what it was, he, with flesh, lowered himself into emptiness, according to what is written, 'He appeared upon the earth, and associated with men,' directing toward sanctification, justifying the one approaching by faith, having opened the gate of the kingdom of the heavens, commending what is beneficial, showing the truth, and the divine light indeed instilling, but through the works of power, that God according to nature is, and if he became flesh, manifest to the opposers he makes.
Therefore also he said, 'If I do not do the works of my Father, do not believe me; but if I do, even if you do not believe me, believe the works.'
For indeed the word was a drawing toward obedience, and the abundance of the theophany greatly toward clear demonstration of the himself according to nature God being.

But it did not seem right to think thus those from Israel, for the Savior of all and Redeemer, with the unto excessive obedience insulting, long times they completed, and dying they crucified, 'evil instead of good giving back to him,' according to what is written, and with the devil's impulses eagerly joining together.
Then therefore he remained among the dead, and having endured with us human death, to the of the impending corruption destructions having fallen into pits? Not at all.
For life he was according to nature, and he lived again three-day, beginning and door and way to the human nature even in this having become.
But since he lived again, having despoiled Hades, toward the in the heavens Father and God he went up.
He will come at the appointed times, as we believe, with the holy angels, and he will sit indeed upon the throne of his glory, and he will distribute to each according to his work.

Therefore let us celebrate, death having been destroyed, and corruption having been abolished, and sin having been beforehand done away with through faith, and the kingdom of heaven being set before us, being awaited and thus hope shining forth.
Since then we shall stand before the judge giving account of the words of our life, let us take care of virtue.
Let us attend to righteousness, love, brotherly affection, gentleness, self-control, and simply every virtue.
Let us look after widows, let us have mercy on orphans, let us attend to those in bodily weaknesses, those in the receiving places let us recover healing, let us attend to prisoners.

Thus then, having cast off every hindrance, and walking upright in faith, let us celebrate purely, beginning from the holy Fast of the fifth of the month of Phamenoth, and the week of the saving Passover from the tenth of the month of Pharmuthi, ending the fasts on the fifteenth of the same month Pharmuthi, in the evening of the deep Sabbath, according to the evangelical proclamation; celebrating also on the following dawning Lord's Day, the sixteenth of the same month, joining also the seven weeks of the holy Pentecost.
Thus then we shall delight in the divine words, in Christ Jesus our Lord, through whom also with the Father and the Holy Spirit, honor and glory and power to the ages.
